messages.text: Compare difference between Carlyle Oceans and National Geographic Adams

Both are 12" illuminated antique-ocean desk globes with raised relief, so they'll feel similar on your desk. The Carlyle is the more budget-friendly choice at $135, while the National Geographic Adams brings the National Geographic cartography and branding at $188 — a nice touch if you like that map style or are gifting to a geography enthusiast.

Is the National Geographic name/style something that matters to you, or are you just after the best illuminated antique look for the price?
I don’t care about National Geographic branding. Does either have better legibility? Any difference in features?

I don't have detailed specs comparing text size or legibility between the two in what's on file — both are listed simply as 12" illuminated antique ocean globes with raised relief. Since branding isn't a factor for you, the Carlyle Illuminated Desk Globe at $135 gives you the same illuminated antique look for less. Want me to point you to that product page?
I want the look, and I want whichever would have the best map readability, and legibility. Does the national geographic have a better defined map for reading ?

I genuinely don't have map-legibility specs for either one in what's on file, so I can't honestly say one reads better than the other. What I can tell you for sure: the Carlyle Illuminated Desk Globe gives you the same illuminated antique ocean look with raised relief for $135, versus $188 for the National Geographic Adams.
